blocks.content: THE INSPIRING LIFE OF STEVE JOBS
GENERAL VO NGUYEN GIAP – A NATIONAL HERO

questions.question: President Ho Chi Minh ______ his whole life to the struggle for national independence and freedom.
Dang Thuy Tram was a young surgeon who volunteered to work in the ______ during the resistance war.
Steve Jobs was widely recognized as a ______ leader whose innovations transformed the technology industry.
After struggling with a severe illness for several years, the renowned poet ______ at the age of 75.
Although he ______ of college after only one semester, he continued auditing classes that interested him.
International students often experience ______ when they first move to a country with very different customs.
Preserving traditional festivals is an effective way for ethnic groups to maintain their cultural ______.

Traditional Vietnamese ______ is famous for its harmonious balance of fresh herbs, spices, and natural flavors.
In some cultures, pointing your index finger directly at someone is considered a serious ______.
Cycling or taking public transport instead of driving private cars helps reduce our ______ footprint.
Before putting glass jars and plastic bottles into the recycling bin, you should ______ them out thoroughly.
Plastic bags and styrofoam boxes take hundreds of years to ______ in natural environments.

a. An: Why don't we organize a 'Green Exchange Day' where students swap old books and clothes for small potted plants?
b. Binh: We need to come up with a practical activity for our school's Green Living Week next month.
c. An: Exactly! And we can also set up a booth to teach students how to make compost from fruit peels.
d. Binh: I love that! Let's write a proposal and submit it to our youth union teacher this afternoon.
e. Binh: That sounds wonderful! It will encourage reusing items and reduce landfill waste at the same time.

Dear Ben,
a. Last weekend, while I was visiting the Vietnam Military History Museum, I learned a lot about General Vo Nguyen Giap.
b. If you ever visit Ha Noi, I will definitely take you to this museum to explore more about his life.
c. I hope you and your family are doing well in Melbourne.
d. Although he never received formal military training at an academy, his strategic genius led our nation to historic victories.
e. His humility and lifelong devotion to the country truly left a deep impression on me.
Best wishes,
Quang

Dear Yumiko,
a. There will be traditional food stalls, folk games like tug of war, and musical performances from ten different countries.
b. I am writing to invite you to the International Cultural Festival at our school next Saturday morning.
c. Please let me know by Thursday if you can make it so I can register your name at the gate.
d. Since you are interested in multicultural traditions, I thought this event would be a fantastic experience for you.
e. You can even wear your traditional kimono and share stories about Japanese festivals with our classmates.
Warm regards,
Phuong

Dear Mr. Harrison,
a. Currently, hundreds of single-use plastic cups and straws are thrown away in our school canteen every single day.
b. On behalf of the Green Living Club, I am writing to propose a campaign to reduce plastic waste on our campus.
c. We look forward to hearing your thoughts and hope to receive your approval for this initiative.
d. To tackle this problem, we suggest installing water refill stations and providing discounts for students who bring reusable bottles.
e. Not only will this plan cut down on landfill waste, but it will also raise students' environmental awareness in the long run.
Sincerely,
Nguyen Minh

a. During the resistance war, she volunteered to work as a battlefield surgeon in Quang Ngai Province.
b. Born into a family of medical professionals in Ha Noi, Dang Thuy Tram graduated from medical university in 1966.
c. Today, her diary has been translated into over twenty languages and continues to inspire young generations worldwide.
d. While she was tending to wounded soldiers under fierce bombings, she recorded her thoughts and ideals in a small diary.
e. Sadly, she was killed in action in 1970 when she was only twenty-seven years old.

a. Reading biographies of admirable figures offers numerous benefits for young people's personal growth.
b. First, learning how great leaders and scientists overcame failures teaches teenagers resilience and determination.
c. Moreover, stories of selfless devotion inspire youths to live responsibly and contribute to their communities.
d. When students see that even geniuses faced self-doubt and hardship, they become less afraid of making mistakes.
e. In conclusion, admirable life stories serve as powerful guiding lights that help shape strong character and ambition.

a. However, this rapid integration also poses a risk of losing distinct local traditions among younger generations.
b. Globalization has transformed the modern world into a vibrant multicultural village.
c. People can now easily enjoy Korean pop music, Italian pasta, or Japanese sushi right in their hometowns.
d. Therefore, while embracing global trends, every nation must actively preserve its unique cultural identity.
e. Such exposure to diverse lifestyles fosters mutual understanding and reduces cultural prejudices.

a. At first, newcomers often feel excited by the novel sights, sounds, and cuisines of the host country.
b. Moving to a foreign country for study or work often triggers a psychological process known as culture shock.
c. Fortunately, by learning the local language and keeping an open mind, most people eventually adapt and feel at home.
d. As the initial excitement fades, however, language barriers and unfamiliar customs can cause frustration and homesickness.
e. Simple daily tasks, such as using public transport or ordering food, may suddenly seem overwhelming.

a. Next, add a layer of green waste, such as vegetable scraps and fruit peels, on top of the brown layer.
b. Making organic compost at home is a simple yet effective way to recycle kitchen leftovers.
c. First, prepare a ventilated bin and place a layer of brown materials like dry leaves and shredded cardboard at the bottom.
d. After a few months of regular turning, the mixture will decompose into dark, nutrient-rich soil for your garden.
e. Remember to sprinkle a little water occasionally to keep the pile moist and speed up decomposition.

a. Furthermore, turning off lights and unplugging electronic devices when not in use significantly lowers electricity consumption.
b. Adopting a green lifestyle does not require drastic sacrifices; instead, it begins with small daily habits.
c. By practicing these simple eco-friendly actions consistently, everyone can help protect the planet in the long run.
d. For instance, carrying a reusable water bottle and cloth bag can eliminate hundreds of single-use plastics each year.
e. This reduction in energy demand directly decreases the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere.

questions.question:
Where in paragraph 1 does the following sentence best fit?
"Despite these harsh living conditions, she graduated first in her physics degree and second in mathematics."
The word "perseverance" in paragraph 2 is CLOSEST in meaning to ______.
The word "it" in paragraph 3 refers to ______.
According to paragraph 2, how did Marie Curie honor her native country?
options: She returned to Poland immediately after graduating from the Sorbonne.
She named one of the newly discovered radioactive elements after Poland.
She donated all of her 1903 Nobel Prize money to Polish universities.
She built a modern physics laboratory in Warsaw with Pierre Curie.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes paragraph 4?
options: The reasons why scientists in the early twentieth century ignored the dangers of radiation.
Curie's humanitarian service during World War I and the fatal health cost of her scientific work.
The technical difficulties of manufacturing mobile X-ray vehicles for the French military.
How Marie Curie trained female doctors to perform complex surgeries on the battlefield.

questions.question: The word "indelible" in paragraph 4 is OPPOSITE in meaning to ______.
Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
options: Marie Curie patented the radium-isolation process to fund her mobile radiography units.
Pierre Curie shared the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with his wife.
Marie and Pierre Curie conducted their research on pitchblende in a state-of-the-art laboratory.
Marie Curie worked as a governess to support her sister's education before studying in Paris.

questions.question: Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 3?
options: She gave up her research into radioactivity in 1911 due to widespread gender bias at the Sorbonne.
Winning the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911 helped her eliminate all gender prejudice in French universities.
Even though male academics discriminated against her, she persisted with her pioneering studies and earned another Nobel Prize in 1911.
Because the academic community strongly supported female scientists, she easily won her second Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.

questions.question: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Marie Curie was fully aware of the fatal effects of radiation when she first discovered radium.
Her sister Bronislawa broke her promise to help Marie move to Paris for university.
Marie Curie valued scientific progress and human welfare far more than personal wealth.
Women in nineteenth-century France were not allowed to study science at the Sorbonne.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the passage?
options: World War I accelerated the development of medical X-ray technology across European battlefields.
Overcoming poverty, loss, and prejudice, Marie Curie devoted her life to pioneering science and humanitarian service.
The partnership between Marie and Pierre Curie proved that teamwork is essential for winning Nobel Prizes.

Financial hardship in nineteenth-century Poland forced many talented young women to emigrate to France.
]

questions.question:
Where in paragraph 2 does the following sentence best fit?
"Such openness to foreign celebrations does not necessarily weaken local traditions when practiced mindfully."
The word "tolerance" in paragraph 2 is CLOSEST in meaning to ______.
The word "they" in paragraph 3 refers to ______.
According to paragraph 1, what role do folk games and shared rituals play in communities?
options: They encourage young people to abandon rural villages for big cities.
They reinforce people's feeling of connection and belonging to their community.
They generate significant advertising revenue for multinational corporations.
They replace formal history lessons in secondary and high schools.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes paragraph 3?
options: The reasons why shopping malls offer big discounts during Halloween and Lunar New Year.
The negative impacts of commercialization and superficial consumption on the true meaning of traditional festivals.
How international tourism provides financial support to preserve sacred ceremonies in developing countries.
Why social media photography has become the most popular extracurricular activity among teenagers.

questions.question: The word "innovative" in paragraph 4 is OPPOSITE in meaning to ______.
Which of the following is NOT TRUE according to the passage?
options: Some sacred rituals are modified in tourist areas to fit visitors' schedules.
Digital platforms can be used to educate young people about the meaning of ancient customs.
Traditional festivals help transmit folklore and moral values across generations.
Celebrating foreign holidays like Halloween automatically causes students to forget Tet traditions.

questions.question: Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 4?
options: Contemporary trends have completely replaced ancient rituals in interactive workshops and online platforms.
Young people prefer attending online workshops rather than participating in real-life traditional festivals.
Rather than banning modern influences, organizers employ technology and hands-on activities to teach the true meaning of traditional customs.
Cultural organizers prohibit the use of digital media during festivals so that ancient rituals remain completely unchanged.

questions.question: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Traditional festivals can only survive if communities isolate themselves from globalization.
Young generations are no longer interested in celebrating Lunar New Year with their families.
Education about the origins of customs is key to preventing festivals from becoming hollow commercial events.
International tourists should be banned from attending local religious ceremonies.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the passage?
options: Schools should stop celebrating foreign festivals to protect students from experiencing culture shock.
Traditional festivals foster cultural identity and global understanding, but they must be protected from over-commercialization through meaningful education.
Global media and tourism have turned local holidays like Diwali and Día de los Muertos into worldwide shopping events.

Folk games such as tug of war and bamboo dancing are the only aspects of traditional festivals worth preserving.
]

questions.question:
Where in paragraph 2 does the following sentence best fit?
"This massive water consumption places severe stress on agricultural communities in arid regions."
The word "staggering" in paragraph 2 is CLOSEST in meaning to ______.
The word "they" in paragraph 3 refers to ______.
According to paragraph 3, how do synthetic clothes pollute the oceans even before being thrown away?
options: They block sewage pipes in coastal cities when people flush them down toilets.
They release tiny plastic fibers into wastewater whenever they are washed at home.
They absorb toxic chemical dyes from rivers during the manufacturing process.
They consume 2,700 liters of seawater for every garment produced.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes paragraph 2?
options: Why cotton farming is more profitable than synthetic fiber manufacturing.
The severe impact of clothing production on global carbon emissions and water resources.
How maritime shipping and international aviation reduce their carbon footprints.
New technologies used by textile factories to purify chemical wastewater.

questions.question: The word "vital" in paragraph 4 is OPPOSITE in meaning to ______.
Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
options: The fashion industry produces fewer carbon emissions than international aviation.
Second-hand clothing platforms are unpopular among environmentally conscious young people.
Fast-fashion brands only release four clothing collections each year.
Polyester fabrics take centuries to break down in landfills because they are made from fossil fuels.

questions.question: Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 4?
options: Fashion brands must force customers to return their old clothes before they are allowed to purchase new collections.
Durable clothing made from recycled materials is too expensive for average shoppers to afford.
Shoppers can greatly reduce the environmental impact of their clothes by buying long-lasting items, exchanging garments, and favoring recycled fabrics.
Unless consumers stop buying clothes altogether, recycling and swapping outfits will have no effect on their carbon footprint.

questions.question: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Natural cotton production has zero negative impact on the environment.
Fast fashion will disappear within the next year without any effort from consumers.
Consumer purchasing habits have a direct influence on the volume of textile waste sent to landfills.
Washing synthetic clothes in cold water completely eliminates microplastic pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the passage?
options: Governments should ban all textile dyeing factories to protect rivers from chemical contamination.
Fast fashion causes severe carbon, water, and plastic pollution, making mindful and sustainable clothing choices essential.
The invention of synthetic polyester has made modern clothing much cheaper and more durable than cotton.

Charity shops have replaced traditional clothing stores as the largest sector of the global apparel industry.
]
